rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two candidate flags checked and cleared. (a) chunk 1, line 200: "The diagnose-and-re-send you just ran was exactly this move" — names the exercise by its slug-title (not merely located), and this lecture's own maintainer block + Lecture meta ("In-room close after Debrief") place it directly after the diagnose-and-resend exercise, so the module-arc-beats-in-openers/closers carve-out applies. (b) chunk 2, line 210: "Geoffrey Huntley's Ralph is the one published practice that runs all three at once" uses "all three" before this file itself has enumerated three pieces (plan.md and the verifier are named later, chunk 2 and chunk 3). Checked against `curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` (grep -n "three" — line 15: "read the failed run through three failure-mode lenses"; line 176: "three-verifier-shapes"): the exercise the student just ran already established the three-piece/three-lens frame, so "all three" resolves via the arc-earned/session-carryover route this lecture is placed to use, not as a dangling forward reference. Harm check: the rule guards against a reader losing the thread of a live antecedent; here the antecedent was set an hour earlier in the room, which is exactly what the carve-out exists to permit.

The one cross-material reference ("the diagnose-and-re-send you just ran", chunk 1 line 200) names the source by its title/slug rather than locating it by position ("the previous exercise"). All other citations (Huntley, Ronacher, Klaassen, Kim/Cherny, Curran) are external practitioner attributions with names attached, not positional pointers into another repo file.

Every chunk (1-9) carries at least one self-contained claim beyond a bare wait-state bullet: e.g. chunk 4 "Hooks always fire" (lines 221-225) states the hook-fires-unconditionally claim in its own two bullets; chunk 9 (lines 252-257) states the Intercom-tier claim standalone. Checked each of the 9 headers against its chunk body: e.g. "Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste" (line 226) is answered exactly by its own bullet "Must happen goes in a hook; recommended stays in a prompt or rule" (line 228); "At org scale: Intercom's tiers" (line 252) is answered by the tiered-review-structure content that follows. No header is contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked all five sub-items against the full body: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction found; no anaphora/epistrophe triples found; no self-grading superlative (e.g. "one of the most useful") found anywhere in the body; the only stated numbers (19.2%, 14.6 min, 75.8 min, 86%, ~500; roughly 80%/20%) are asserted plainly and never retracted or hedged into vagueness; no abstraction-noun-stack phrasing or empty-leg verb triplets found. No content-level presence gap to flag here.
